Good News, Everyone! by Leo Pinheiro
anybody know why it's got that title? I know just barely enough about futurama to have recognized the cast (barely), but not enough to inform the title...

Professor Farnsworth (Fry's great-great-great-great-great-great-grandson) always comes to the show's cast (a delivery crew), usually at the start of an episode saying "good news, everyone" - and then tell them about their latest delivery assignment, usually to an extremely dangerous and potentially lethal mission - so it's basically an irony thing to get every episode going. It's "good news" because they got a job to keep them from going bankrupt for another day but it's hardly real good news if it means everyone could die or be seriously injured at the very least.

Since it happens almost on every single episode it is also a meta-joke at some points. On one episode for example Fry is gone from the crew to become a cop and the Professor comes in and tells the crew about the next delivery - when he finishes someone asks did you forget to say "good news, everyone"? and he replies that he was only doing it all this time to make Fry feel better about regularly leaving on suicide missions. Or in a few other episodes the Professor is gone and someone says the line in his place (usually mimicking the exact way he says it, in an elderly voice an all) or the phrase is used out of context, etc.

Source: have been watching the last seasons lately, since I stopped watching the show when it was first canceled, been having a blast at it! There are one or two episodes they tried to become more a Family Guy random-stupid humor show but luckily it was quickly over. Absolutely recommend it to you, great show, a lot better than Groening's Simpson for me!
